description: A screen copy of an Akai MIDIMix: every knob, fader and button on the controller gets a control here and an output jack, and the module drives the controller's button lamps back the other way

params.text: Follows one of the controller's 24 knobs and can be turned on screen as well; the hardware knob has no motor, so turning this one leaves the controller where it was until its next message arrives
Follows one of the controller's eight channel faders and can be moved on screen as well; the hardware fader has no motor, so moving this one leaves the controller where it was
Latches that strip's mute on and off; the matching lamp on the controller is driven to match, and pressing the controller's own button toggles it too
Latches that strip's record arm on and off; the matching lamp on the controller is driven to match, and pressing the controller's own button toggles it too
Follows the controller's ninth fader and can be moved on screen as well
Latches one of the controller's two bank buttons on and off, with the lamp under that button driven to match
Latches the controller's solo button on and off; that button has no lamp in the hardware, so only the screen shows its state

outputs.text: 10V while that strip's mute is latched on, 0V while it is off
10V while that strip's record arm is latched on, 0V while it is off
10V while that switch is latched on, 0V while it is off

notes: nothing arrives until a device is chosen: right-click and set both the MIDI input and the MIDI output to the MIDI Mix, because the output is what drives the lamps
the controller never lights its own buttons, so this module holds the true button state and resends all eighteen lamps periodically; unplugging and replugging the controller resyncs on its own
after loading a patch, press SEND ALL on the controller to push its knob and fader positions into the module, which cannot ask for them itself
the red lamp at the top of the panel brightens whenever a MIDI message arrives and fades over about an eighth of a second, which is the quickest way to tell whether the device is talking
menu: MIDI input (MIDIMix) — heads the chooser for the port the controller's knob, fader and button messages come in on
MIDI output (LEDs) — heads the chooser for the port the button lamp messages are sent out on; set it to the same device
Jitter filter (dead-band) — drops single-step changes from a noisy pot but accepts both extremes, so the full travel stays reachable
